title: Proactive upgrade lifecycle briefing & customer-facing rollback playbook
creator: Evelyn Park
description:
Summary:
Create a concise, multi-channel customer upgrade briefing and an embedded rollback playbook that product, support, and account teams can use during the LTS 2026.01 upgrade window. This ticket delivers a set of customer-facing artifacts: a phased notification schedule (90/60/30/14/7/1 days), a short-form public changelog template, a technical migration one-pager (for platform engineers), an opt-in/auto-upgrade FAQ, and a one-click rollback checklist for Dedicated & Private customers.

Audience:
- Primary: customers on Dedicated or Private deployments and their platform/infra teams.
- Secondary: hosted customers with production workloads (for awareness only).

Why this is needed:
- Recent runtime-1.19 -> 1.20 changes introduce kernel scheduling defaults and a KV-cache behavior change that may affect tail-latency for some query shapes. We must: 1) set clear expectations, 2) provide pre-checks and mitigations, 3) enable safe automatic rollbacks and make them discoverable to customers and CS/SEs.

Scope & Deliverables:
- Public-facing brief (short): 250–400 word summary that appears in release notes and support portal.
- Detailed migration one-pager: compatibility matrix (model variants, quantization profiles, client SDK versions), pre-upgrade checks, and common troubleshooting steps.
- Email templates: three variants (Enterprise announcement, Technical ops bulletin, and Executive summary). Each with placeholders and recommended send cadence.
- Changelog template: "What changed", "Why we changed it", "Who is impacted", "Migration steps", "Rollback instructions".
- Rollback playbook (customer-facing): step-by-step rollback for Dedicated/Private with safety checks and SLAs, including links to console actions, GitHub ops runbook, and support escalation path.
- Internal playbook: CS/SE triage checklist, suggested support responses, and canned runbook entries for both planned and emergency rollbacks.
- Measurement plan: CTR on email, open rates, time-to-rollback, number of incidents after upgrade (target: <= 1 per 100 tenants), and CS escalations.

Links to artifacts / references:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/LTS+2026.01+Upgrade+Briefing
- Design doc (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3-example
- Docs PR (prose + changelog): https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412
- Runtime release notes draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/releases/tag/v1.20.0-rc

Out-of-scope:
- Changes to the runtime itself (handled in ENG tickets). We focus on customer communication and runbooks only.

Acceptance criteria:
- Finalized email templates (enterprise/ops/executive) reviewed by Legal and Support.
- Public brief and detailed migration one-pager published to Docs site and linked from the Console upgrade modal.
- Rollback playbook validated with ENG runbook (ENG-9010) and tested in staging (proof: internal runbook test log link).
- CS/SE training doc and one internal triage session completed and recorded.
- Measurement hooks instrumented (links to dashboard) and baseline metrics collected prior to rollout.
deliverables: Public changelog template and sample entry
Internal CS/SE triage checklist and training recording
Measurement dashboard link and baseline metrics
acceptance_criteria: 1) All customer-facing artifacts published under release docs and linked from the Console. 2) Legal approval recorded in PR discussion. 3) Rollback playbook exercised in staging with one successful rollback test documented. 4) CS/SE readout completed and one Q&A session held. 5) Dashboard confirms measurement hooks are recording upgrade metrics.

communication_plan: Phase schedule: 90-day heads-up (product blog + docs), 60-day technical bulletin (email to technical contacts), 30-day migration checklist + console banner, 14/7/1-day reminder emails, Day-of upgrade broadcast and post-upgrade status page update. Channels: email, Console banner, status.redwood.ai, in-product changelog drawer, and account manager outreach for high-touch customers.
metrics_and_kpis: Email open rate >= 35% for technical bulletin, Migration checklist completion >= 60% for opt-in customers, Time-to-rollback median < 20 minutes (for Dedicated), Number of post-upgrade incidents <= 1 per 100 tenants in first 72 hours.
